page: Microsoft Azure FX4-2ms_v2 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the FXmsv2 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. This instance features 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at a high base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. It is equipped with 84.0 GB of system memory, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 42.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for deep learning and mathematical operations. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The high-frequency 4.2 GHz Intel processor delivers top-tier single-core performance, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2333.0 and strong single-threaded compression and decompression rates. However, due to the physical constraint of having only one physical core with two threads, multi-core and parallelized workloads perform poorly, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2897.0 and a weak Passmark CPU score of 4164.68. Memory bandwidth also shows limitations under large block sizes, with read and write speeds falling into the poor category, though small-block cached reads reach 172.01 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the FX4-2ms_v2 represents a highly specialized resource allocation. It trades massive parallel processing power for a dense memory footprint and high single-threaded clock speeds. This makes it an inefficient choice for highly parallelized compute tasks, multi-threaded compilation, or heavy database operations, which scored poorly in Passmark database tests. Instead, the instance is best suited for memory-intensive, single-threaded workloads, legacy applications that cannot scale horizontally but require massive RAM, or lightweight text processing and low-concurrency web serving.
